s1.syndrome_frame: A subcutaneous mass with recent growth and tenderness on the lower leg
salient_findings: Painful nodule on the lower part of the right leg
Enlargement and tenderness of the lesion over the past 6 months
Irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass
key_facts: 40-year-old man
Lesion initially stable in size and painless for 4 years
No history of trauma
No personal or family history of malignancy
Mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Normal routine blood tests
Negative tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV
Lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass on gross examination
Dermal tumor extending into the superficial subcutis
Nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells on light microscopy
Strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45 on immunohistochemical staining

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a subcutaneous mass with recent growth and tenderness, and immunohistochemical staining shows strong positivity for vimentin

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could present as a subcutaneous mass, but less likely given the lack of HIV or immunosuppression history

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the spindle-shaped cells, but less common in this location

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the subcutaneous location, but the histological description is not typical

shortlist.label: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the histological description, but less common in this location and age group

raw.rationale: The tumor's characteristics, such as a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass with nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells and strong positivity for vimentin, are consistent with Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans. The tumor's location on the lower part of the leg and its initial stability in size and painlessness for 4 years also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's negative HIV test and lack of other suspicious cutaneous lesions make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: The tumor cells' morphology and immunohistochemical staining pattern do not support a diagnosis of leiomyosarcoma.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: The tumor's microscopic features, such as nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells, do not resemble those of liposarcoma.

rejected.label: Malignant fibrous histiocytoma
rejected.why: The tumor's characteristics, such as its location and microscopic features, are not typical of malignant fibrous histiocytoma.
